[1] The patient presented with syncope and collapse, facial weakness, and urinary incontinence.
[2] The primary diagnosis was syncope and collapse.
[3] Active diagnoses included atrial fibrillation, other specified cardiac dysrhythmias, head injury, unspecified, cervicalgia, unspecified visual disturbance, urinary tract infection, unspecified, other and unspecified Escherichia coli, acute kidney failure, unspecified, hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified, chronic kidney disease, Stage III (moderate), diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled, polyneuropathy in diabetes, depressive disorder, not elsewhere classified, esophageal reflux, unspecified vitamin D deficiency, other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites, neurogenic bladder NOS, osteoarthrosis, unspecified whether generalized or localized, pelvic region and thigh, and other and unspecified hyperlipidemia.
[4] Past medical history included long-term (current) use of anticoagulants, history of fall, personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy, and other acquired absence of organ.
[5] Procedures were none.
[6] Medications included Simvastatin 20mg PO/NG, Warfarin 1mg PO/NG, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3mL IV, Ciprofloxacin HCl 500mg PO/NG, Acetaminophen 500mg PO/NG, Influenza Virus Vaccine 0.5mL IM, Glucose Gel 15g PO, Omeprazole 20mg PO, Vitamin D 1000UNIT PO/NG, Glucagon 1mg IM, Bag 1BAG IV, Magnesium Sulfate 2gm IV, Citalopram 20mg PO/NG, Ferrous Sulfate 325mg PO/NG, Insulin 0UNIT SC, and Dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV.

[8] Services included MED.
[9] The patient was admitted to the Emergency Department and Med/Surg ward.
[10] The patient was discharged alive.
